[[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] incumbent [[Josh Hawley]] was re-elected to a second term, defeating [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee [[Lucas Kunce]]. Primary elections took place on August 6, 2024.{{Cite web |title=2024 State Primary Election Dates |url=https://www.ncsl.org/elections-and-campaigns/2024-state-primary-election-dates |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=www.ncsl.org}} Hawley was the favorite in the polls throughout the cycle due to the state's Republican lean, though some polls showed a close race.{{Cite web |date=2024-10-25 |title=New poll finds Hawley leading Kunce by wide margin in Missouri Senate race |url=https://fox4kc.com/politics/new-poll-finds-hawley-leading-kunce-by-wide-margin-in-missouri-senate-race/ |access-date=2024-11-16 |website=FOX 4 Kansas City WDAF-TV {{!}} News, Weather, Sports |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Wiederkehr |first=Ryan Best, Aaron Bycoffe, Ritchie King, Dhrumil Mehta and Anna |date=2018-06-28 |title=Missouri : U.S. Senate : 2024 Polls |url=https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/polls/senate/2024/missouri/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231109231029/https://projects.fivethirtyeight.com/polls/senate/2024/missouri/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 9, 2023 |access-date=2024-11-16 |website=FiveThirtyEight |language=en}} Kunce, who had previously run in [[2022 United States Senate election in Missouri#Democratic primary|2022]], losing narrowly in the Democratic primaries to Trudy Busch Valentine, was seen as a strong candidate who outpaced Hawley in fundraising for much of the race and outspent him in advertising.{{Cite news |date=2022-08-02 |title=Missouri Primary Election Results |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2022/08/02/us/elections/results-missouri.html |access-date=2024-11-16 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}{{Cite web |last=Hancock |first=Jason |date=2024-10-16 |title=Democrat Lucas Kunce outraises Missouri Republican Sen. Josh Hawley • Missouri Independent |url=https://missouriindependent.com/2024/10/16/democrat-lucas-kunce-outraises-missouri-republican-sen-josh-hawley/ |access-date=2024-11-16 |website=Missouri Independent |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Hancock |first=Jason |title=Democrat Lucas Kunce raises twice as much money as incumbent Republican Josh Hawley |url=https://www.news-leader.com/story/news/politics/elections/2024/10/19/lucas-kunce-outraises-incumbent-josh-hawley-in-senate-race/75720541007/ |access-date=2024-11-16 |website=Springfield News-Leader |language=en-US}} Hawley ultimately won re-election with a comfortable 55.6% of the vote to Kunce's 41.8%, improving his 2018 margin by around 8 points. Nonetheless, the race was roughly 5 points closer than the [[2024 United States presidential election in Missouri|concurrent presidential election]].{{Cite web |last=Baker |first=Michael |title=Presidential election results 2024 {{!}} CNN Politics |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2024/results/president?admin1=29&election-data-id=2024-PG&selected-election-data-id=2024-PG-MO&election-painting-mode=projection-with-lead&filter-key-races=false&filter-flipped=false&filter-remaining=false |access-date=2024-11-16 |website=CNN |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Riley |first=Emily |title=Senate election results 2024 {{!}} CNN Politics |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2024/results/senate?admin1=29&election-data-id=2024-SG&selected-election-data-id=2024-SG-MO&election-painting-mode=projection-with-lead&filter-key-races=false&filter-flipped=false&filter-remaining=false |access-date=2024-11-16 |website=CNN |language=en}}{{toclimit|3}} == Background == From [[1904 United States presidential election|1904]] to [[2004 United States presidential election|2004]], Missouri's electoral votes always went to the winner of the presidential race, with only one exception: in [[1956 United States presidential election|1956]], during the landslide re-election of President [[Dwight D. Eisenhower|Dwight Eisenhower]], Missouri went to [[Illinois]] [[Governor of Illinois|Governor]] [[Adlai Stevenson II|Adlai Stevenson]]. The state's accuracy in voting with the national consensus includes the highly competitive elections of [[1960 United States presidential election|1960]], [[1976 United States presidential election|1976]], and [[2000 United States presidential election|2000]].{{Cite web |title=Missouri Presidential Election Voting History - 270toWin |url=https://www.270towin.com/states/Missouri |access-date=2024-07-01 |website=270toWin.com}} Missouri is no longer thought of as a perennial swing state, and is today considered to be a strongly [[red states and blue states|red]] state. Since 1960, the only three Democrats it has backed have been Southerners: [[Lyndon B. Johnson]], [[Jimmy Carter]], and [[Bill Clinton]]. In [[2008 United States presidential election|2008]], Missouri narrowly voted for the losing candidate, Republican [[John McCain]], despite a sizable [[United States electoral college|electoral college]] win for Democrat [[Barack Obama]]. In [[2012 United States presidential election|2012]], Missouri favored losing candidate [[Mitt Romney]] by nearly 10 percentage points, despite another significant victory for Obama in the rest of the country. In [[2016 United States presidential election|2016]] and [[2020 United States presidential election|2020]], Missouri again voted strongly Republican, this time for [[Donald Trump]] by over 15 points, despite Trump losing the latter election. This marked the third time in four presidential elections that Missouri supported a losing Republican. Missouri has not supported any Democratic candidate since Bill Clinton in [[1996 United States presidential election in Missouri|1996]]. In more recent years, Republicans have experienced significant electoral success in the state. In [[2016 Missouri elections|2016]], the Republican Party secured victories in key statewide positions, including [[List of governors of Missouri|Governor]], [[Attorney General of Missouri|Attorney General]], [[Secretary of State of Missouri|Secretary of State]], and [[State Treasurer of Missouri|Treasurer]]. Building on this momentum, in [[2022 Missouri State Auditor election|2022]], [[Scott Fitzpatrick]] successfully won the position of [[State Auditor of Missouri|Auditor]], a seat previously held by Democrat [[Nicole Galloway]]. Notably, Nicole Galloway remains the last Democrat to have been elected to a statewide position in the state.{{Cite web |title=Nicole Galloway |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Nicole_Galloway |access-date=2024-07-01 |website=Ballotpedia |language=en}} The most recent Democrat to secure election to the Senate from Missouri was [[Claire McCaskill]] back in [[2012 United States Senate election in Missouri|2012]]. She sought a third term in [[2018 United States Senate election in Missouri|2018]], facing off against [[Josh Hawley]], but was ultimately defeated by a margin of 5.8%.{{Cite web |title=Missouri {{!}} Full Senate results |url=https://www.cnn.com/election/2018/results/missouri |access-date=2024-07-01 |website=www.cnn.com |language=en}} Most pollsters categorized this race as safe for the Republican Party. == Republican primary == === Candidates === ==== Nominee ==== *[[Josh Hawley]], incumbent U.S. senator{{Cite web |url=https://www.kcur.org/politics-elections-and-government/2023-01-20/early-jockeying-for-senate-seats-foreshadows-competitive-2024-elections |title=Hawley on the ballot: The 2024 Senate elections are already getting competitive |publisher=[[NPR]] |website=[[KCUR-FM|KCUR]] 89.3 |last=Jones |first=Dustin |date=January 20, 2023 |access-date=May 22, 2023}} ===Endorsements=== {{Endorsements box | title = Josh Hawley | width = 50em | list = '''Organizations''' *[[AIPAC]]{{Cite web|title=Support Pro-Israel Candidates |url=https://candidates.aipacpac.org/page/featured/ |access-date=2023-03-31 |language=en |website=[[AIPAC]]}} *[[Senate Conservatives Fund]]{{Cite web |title=Senate Conservatives Fund |url=https://www.senateconservatives.com/#candidates |access-date=2023-09-02 |website=www.senateconservatives.com}} }} ===Fundraising=== {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! colspan=4 |Campaign finance reports as of July 31, 2024 |- style="text-align:center;" !Candidate !Raised !Spent !Cash on hand |- |{{party shading/Republican}}|Josh Hawley (R) |$22,492,767 |$17,267,201 |$5,701,081 |- ! colspan="4" |Source: [[Federal Election Commission]]{{cite web |title=2024 Election United States Senate -
